items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: We had one saxophone. We used to harmonize. Me and Kenneth, we harmonize.

ctx.x: And we had a nice, a long time. Did you used to call that for any particular reason?

Yeah, more for home. More for that, you know what I mean? Yeah. We had one saxophone. We used to harmonize. Me and Kenneth, we harmonize. We never posted, we never, never prayed straight to you. You know what I mean? The melody. Yeah. Always. I take the melody, he prayed to say, you know what I mean? The harmony, you know? That's why we got by, you see. But see George, George never read. Yeah. But still he had one for him. He was a teacher in the class. He was a teacher. You know what I mean? Yeah. That's what…

You were talking about this drummer without fingers? Yeah, Pete Masarini. He played drums and he had his fingers with all little nubs. The way he used to hold them would get a kick out. Yeah, he was good huh? Yeah, Pete Masarini. He was a joke.
